title: Publish representative JLSE evidence and revised working paper
body:
Superseded by [library PR9](https://github.com/nscottnichols/ffmt/pull/9) and [evaluation PR1](https://github.com/nscottnichols/ffmt-evaluation/pull/1). Do not merge this mixed-history branch. Original description follows.

Publish the representative JLSE campaign with exact source snapshots, per-case outcomes, raw-log hashes and reproducible selection. The report keeps failed terminal configurations and unfinished campaign scope visible. It covers 41 terminal configurations across Rome x86_64, GH200 Arm/CUDA, A40 CUDA, MI300X HIP and Intel Max SYCL/SPIR-V, including OpenMP, Kokkos, AdaptiveCpp and chipStar routes.

The independent oracle remains fmt `0fc31633e7d53ac895ae0a688b83b7d44f0b0c1f`. The primary corpus has 54 stdout cases and 8,216 numeric input records; focused wrapper captures have explicitly smaller stdout selections. Original baseline evidence uses its earlier 40-case corpus. Published measurements retain 768 measured groups and 112 resource probes from 20 selected runs, with separate historical/current source proofs.

Add standalone AMD/NVIDIA OpenMP controls, a generated-table working manuscript and PDF, and scripts to reproduce publication. The supplied outline remains preserved as historical input. The gap ledger records stdout NUL transport limits, execution/JIT and compilation timeouts, the isolated AMD OpenMP callback failure, and a distinct unresolved NVIDIA numeric failure. Results do not imply complete fmt support. Final qualification used A40 for the h100 profile; original-baseline H100 execution remains separately identified.

Validation:

- 25 harness regression tests pass.
- Final committed-library integration: 15/15 CTest entries, Make legacy/fast-math checks, 123 diagnostic-aware negative tests and three positive controls pass.
- GCC13 ASan/UBSan positive suites pass at both -O0 and -O2; negative subprocesses retain their recorded compiler-default optimization.
- Source coverage: 3,445/3,740 executable lines and 2,119/2,540 branch edges, excluding uninstantiated templates and device-only bodies.
- Manuscript builds twice with PDFLaTeX and generated evidence tables; reading copy inspected.

Stacked on #6; earlier focused implementation PRs are #1–#5. Raw installations and runs remain ignored under software/ and artifacts/. The standalone callback source deliberately preserves its tested bytes, including one inherited trailing space, so its published hash remains exact.

title: Harden qualification lifecycle and measured-source provenance
body:
Superseded by [library PR9](https://github.com/nscottnichols/ffmt/pull/9) and [evaluation PR1](https://github.com/nscottnichols/ffmt-evaluation/pull/1). Do not merge this mixed-history branch. Original description follows.

Compiler timeouts could leave JIT descendants running, and an auxiliary-suite exception could leave a partially exercised configuration marked completed. This change kills the process group on timeout, records stdout progress separately, and marks a configuration terminal only after its requested suites return. Reports retain failed controls, fatal errors and unfinished scope. Failed combined builds and executions are checkpointed before case isolation.

The same qualification workflow now verifies Kokkos GPU selection, pins chipStar's transitive tools and typed-pointer translator adapter, and records actual hardware independently of queue profile names. Focused timing filters keep shortest and explicit-scientific presentations separate; manifests distinguish captured library source, runner source, compile-only resource targets and first-batch timing. An allocation-owned helper checks an isolated committed tree with CMake/CTest, Make and coverage.

Arm compiler overrides are retained, and submission defaults select the baseline only for baseline jobs; head/host/benchmark jobs pin the submitting HEAD unless explicitly overridden. The guide includes explicit A40 queue, architecture and Kokkos-prefix examples.

Validation: 25 Python harness regressions pass, including descendant cleanup and interrupted/failed-control reporting; Python/shell syntax checks pass. Native Kokkos guard smokes and deliberately wrong-space controls were exercised, pinned chipStar provisioning completed, and focused benchmark filters were checked against independent fmt output. The broader captured numerical and performance evidence is published in #7.

title: Preserve mutable formatting and repair native family portability
body:
Superseded by [library PR9](https://github.com/nscottnichols/ffmt/pull/9) and [evaluation PR1](https://github.com/nscottnichols/ffmt-evaluation/pull/1). Do not merge this mixed-history branch. Original description follows.

Preserve argument cv qualifiers through the formatting APIs so mutable custom values, nonconst ranges and move-only joins work without copying or const_cast. Correct family padding to render once into bounded writable pointer buffers, retaining the exact truncated prefix. Left alignment also renders once on streams; right/center streaming explicitly rejects nonreplayable bodies instead of invoking a mutating formatter twice.

Remove runtime chrono recursion rejected by SYCL, repair NVCC range traits/delimiter storage, support noncontiguous registered character ranges, fix Unicode debug precision, and accept chipStar generic printf pointers while retaining CUDA address-space handling. Add two generated device probes for bounded and streaming mutation counts (54 stdout cases total). Strict compiler, OpenMP-table and fast-math fixes were backported to #2 so earlier PRs remain independently testable.

Validation:57,365 core oracle comparisons with sanitizers;218 family,1,625 mutable/move-only/noncontiguous/bounded,34,719 percent-format and six C++23 comparisons pass with strict LLVM22 ASan/UBSan. GCC13 optimized family/range/C++23 checks pass. Focused native CUDA, NVCC and Intel reruns validate chrono/range fixes and8,216 numeric records at O0/O2; the selected committed 54-case qualification is published in #7. The two new probes pass both host modes at both optimization levels and compile with NVCC. Raw source hashes/commands remain in the captured manifests.

Stacked on #4. Final qualification, known backend gaps, measurements and the revised working manuscript are published in #7.

Header separation keeps optional type families out of core consumers.

Expand the independently generated backend corpus from 40 to 52 stdout cases. Family regressions compare full outputs and bounded counts against the pinned fmt oracle: 206 family cases, 34,719 percent-format comparisons and six optional C++23 cases. LLVM22 strict-warning ASan/UBSan validation and native GCC13 optimized validation pass; CMake/CTest integration passes all available suites. The oracle has calendar adapters for older libstdc++ feature macros rather than changing expected output.

Host filesystem/stream/RTTI/locale/timezone services are outside the device surface. Final representative backend qualification is published in #7; a host type adapter does not establish device callability for every standard-library implementation.

Stacked on #2. Mutable generic ranges and move-only iterator joins are implemented in the focused follow-up #5 through preservation of argument cv qualifiers.

title: Unify checked device formatting and stream complete output
body:
Superseded by [library PR9](https://github.com/nscottnichols/ffmt/pull/9) and [evaluation PR1](https://github.com/nscottnichols/ffmt-evaluation/pull/1). Do not merge this mixed-history branch. Original description follows.

Replace the two formatting paths with one sink-based engine. Kernel printing now streams complete output through bounded staging, and bounded memory formatting reports written/required counts without adding a terminator. Runtime and wide formats return checked errors; literal formats are validated at compilation.

Preserve existing print calls and static custom formatters, add formatter contexts and ADL format_as, and correct numeric, Unicode, dynamic-specification and bounds behavior. Portable exact shortest conversion is selected for SPIR-V; native host extended precision is retained. Device transport failures remain explicit, including the measured Intel printf NUL limitation.

Validation: 57,361 core comparisons against the independently built pinned fmt oracle; focused native extended precision (1,276), binary128 (81), BitInt (300 where available), bounded canaries, streaming and legacy hooks. Captured LLVM22 ASan/UBSan runs pass with strict warnings. CMake/CTest passes all available tests on GCC13; installed find_package consumer builds and runs. Both legacy oracle truncation and sanitizer bool suppression are removed. Source coverage now reports all instantiated headers with line/branch/region denominators.

Final representative hardware qualification and known gaps are published in #7; captured snapshots keep their original hashes. Earlier captured CUDA/HIP snapshots passed the 40 core stdout cases and 8,216 sampled numeric records at O0/O2; Intel's optimized portable numeric binary also passes 8,216 records with sufficient JIT startup time. OpenMP numeric execution/resource failures remain under investigation.

Stacked on #1; expanded type families follow separately.

title: Add independent fmt conformance and JLSE qualification infrastructure
body:
Superseded by [library PR9](https://github.com/nscottnichols/ffmt/pull/9) and [evaluation PR1](https://github.com/nscottnichols/ffmt-evaluation/pull/1). Do not merge this mixed-history branch. Its original tip is preserved under `archive/jlse-campaign-20261022`; the [migration ledger](https://github.com/nscottnichols/ffmt-evaluation/blob/evaluation-campaign/docs/provenance/README.md) records source and replacement mappings.

Original description follows.

The existing test harness truncated fmt's expected output to ffmt's capacity and parsed payloads as line-delimited control records. Add an independent byte-level runner that preserves complete expectations, tests compiler rejection reasons, and captures immutable source/oracle identities and actual device execution.

Add isolated JLSE software profiles, Cobalt launch/discovery/provisioning scripts, a shared development skill, CMake/CTest integration, and reproducible baseline reports. The baseline deliberately records unsupported features and failed positive controls as gaps.

Validation: 14 harness regressions passed; CMake configuration and the CTest harness target passed; skill validation, Python compilation, shell syntax, and Cobalt submission dry runs passed. Baseline Rome ran both formatting paths at O0/O2 (110 exact positive matches, 22 mismatches, 28 unsupported cases, and 36 expected negative rejections). Hardware baseline results are retained in the report; implementation fixes follow in stacked PRs.
